result:
The proposed answer is not correct in general, because it assumes only the leading coefficient is constant. The hypothesis r ≥ 1 gives more than that.

The Hilbert series of R = k[V]^G is (by Molien-type reasoning, in the non-modular case) an average over g ∈ G of 1/det(1 − gt). Its poles are at roots of unity.

- At t = 1 the pole has order d. This gives the polynomial part, with constant coefficients.
- At a root of unity ζ ≠ 1, the pole order from g is at most dim of the ζ-eigenspace of g on V*.
- Every g fixes (V*)^G, so g has a fixed space of dimension at least r. The ζ-eigenspace for ζ ≠ 1 therefore has dimension at most d − r.

So the periodic, non-constant contributions only affect coefficients of n^{d−r−1} and lower. The coefficients a_i for i = d−r, …, d−1 are therefore constant. For the indices below d−r, the coefficients can be genuinely periodic, so they are not constant in general.

The set of indices with constant a_i is {d−r, …, d−1}, and its sum is r(2d − r − 1)/2. This equals d − 1 only when r = 1. The proposed answer d − 1 therefore fails for r ≥ 2.

VERDICT: REJECT
